batch: Slovakia — self-supplied photo document discovery (Bratislava kiosk)

documentsRuledOut.sourceName: Ministerstvo vnútra SR (police document-office process), as described by preukaz.sk and pravnenoviny.sk citing the official biometric-capture procedure
documentsRuledOut.notes: Since Slovakia moved to biometric passports (chip-based, per EU rules), facial image, fingerprints and signature are captured live and in person at the oddelenie dokladov (police document department) at the time of application — the applicant does NOT bring or submit a photograph at all. Personal appearance is mandatory. No self-supplied-photo exception was found for domestic applications. EXCEPTION NOTED BUT NOT FULLY VERIFIED: applications filed abroad through a Slovak embassy/consulate may follow a different capture process (embassy consular sections generally still use in-person biometric capture equipment where available, per mzv.sk consular pages for e.g. Oslo/Prague/Brussels), but a documented alternate paper/self-supplied-photo path for embassy or emergency/urgent issuance was not found in this research and should not be assumed — flagged as an open question rather than a confirmed exception. A self-supplied photo is therefore not something a Bratislava kiosk could usefully serve for this document.

documentsRuledOut.sourceName: preukaz.sk ("Nasnímanie podoby"), describing the process under Zákon č. 395/2019 Z.z. o občianskych preukazoch, which was amended to implement EU Regulation 2019/1157 on biometric ID cards
documentsRuledOut.notes: Confirms the hypothesis in the task brief: facial likeness, signature, and (from age 12) fingerprints are captured on the spot at the district police headquarters using biometric equipment when the application is filed — 'you do not need to bring a photograph.' This applies to standard (chip-bearing) ID cards. Separately, MV SR issues a distinct no-photo ID variant ("občiansky preukaz bez podoby tváre") to children under 15 and seniors over 65 without a chip document — but that variant likewise involves no self-supplied photo (it simply omits a photo altogether), so it doesn't create a kiosk opportunity either. No self-supplied-photo path found for any občiansky preukaz variant.

documentsRuledOut.documentType: Vodičský preukaz (domestic driver's license — first issue/renewal/replacement)
documentsRuledOut.sourceName: Aggregator sources (autobazar.eu, finalcd.sk) explicitly citing the legal requirement for personal appearance at the police documents department
documentsRuledOut.notes: The domestic driving license is issued at the same oddelenie dokladov (police documents department) as the passport/ID card, and the law requires the applicant's personal presence specifically so that identity can be verified, a digital photograph taken, and the signature scanned on the spot — no self-supplied photo is submitted or accepted. NOTE: this is distinct from the medzinárodný vodičský preukaz (international driving permit), a separate document that DOES require a self-supplied photo — see documentsConfirmed.

documentsRuledOut.sourceName: Mestská časť Bratislava-Rača, official municipal page listing required documents
documentsRuledOut.notes: This Bratislava municipal district's own page lists only a written application plus presentation of an ID card/passport and the administrative fee — no photograph is mentioned anywhere in the required-items list, for adults or (per this page) generally. Some other sources mention a photo only for a specific children's/short-term permit variant (ages 3-5), not the standard adult rybársky lístok. Ruled out: no photo of any kind (self-supplied or otherwise) is part of the standard process.

documentsUnclear.documentType: Preukaz novinára (journalist/press card — Slovenský syndikát novinárov, SSN)
documentsUnclear.notes: SSN is a private professional union, not a government body, so it sits at the edge of what this research brief calls a "government/institutional process" — included here for completeness since the task explicitly listed press cards as a candidate. Found: SSN issues an international press card (IFJ card) to paying members; the application process collects name, date of birth, nationality, and address by email, and states that "printing of ID cards and photos for the cards is handled by an external service" — language that could mean either (a) the member emails/uploads their own photo and an external vendor prints/laminates the card, or (b) the vendor also handles capturing the photo. The SSN pages found (ssn.sk) did not spell out which, nor did they publish any geometric photo spec (dimensions, head size, etc.). Could not find an SSN page confirming a self-supplied-photo requirement with enough clarity to place this in documentsConfirmed, and it is arguably out of scope anyway as a private-association card rather than a government/institutional one. No requirements checklist recorded given the unresolved basic question.
